commands_used: answer 1. I carry the three seal-stones (Blackrose, Gemin, Kings) of the Kings Gate. Never-Writes-Twice in Nesh-Deeka House, Helstrom, ordered them brought to her. Rivals are the Unbound, who drain trees, and Collector Ennodius Vanin. The Gemin tablet warns not to lift the Eye from the Root. 2. Bring the three stones to Never-Writes-Twice in Helstrom, before anyone goes near the Kings Gate under Teku-Sul Spire. 3. I can give her the stones, or hold them back and ask questions first. I can talk to her about the Unbound and the Eye. 4. I do not understand why the Unbound drain trees, what moans in the Fort Chalkmoth cellar, or how Nesh-Deeka knows of the Unbound. I could ask Never-Writes-Twice.

answer 1. I work for the Toh-Reel-Ka order via Never-Writes-Twice. I am now a Ka-Deelith with a pike and heavier armour. The plan: open the Kings Gate with the three stones, use the Eye in place to heal all trees, then return the stones to her and hunt Cuts-the-Old-Knot, who brews the draught that kills the beast at the Root. 2. Dive to Teku-Sul Spire from Bell Station and go to the Kings Gate. 3. Go straight there, or first look at other leads such as Fort Chalkmoth. I could also doubt her plan, since she dodges questions. 4. I do not understand how the order knows the Unbound movements, what is in the Fort Chalkmoth cellar, or why the Unbound drain trees. She would not say; I might find out by exploring.

answer 1. At the Kings Gate, Cuts-the-Old-Knot says the Toh-Reel-Ka, my order, are the secret warriors of the ruling Xeech-Leel and keep sap-fed dreamers in Fort Chalkmoth to spy through the trees; she was one for nine years. She says healing the Eye would help the dreamers see everything, while lifting it ends the dreams but kills about three in ten trees and villages beneath. 2. Choose whether to fight her or believe her, here at the gate. 3. Fight her (take her tomes, staff, draughts, face the guardian alone) or believe her (she fights the guardian beside me, and the Eye choice stays open). Either way, the final choice at the Eye is mine. 4. I cannot verify her claims about the order, the Xeech-Leel, or Umbriel; I could check by seeing the Fort Chalkmoth cellar myself. I do not know the exact fate of the trees if the Eye is lifted.

answer 1. I chose to believe Cuts-the-Old-Knot that the Toh-Reel-Ka spy through sap-fed dreamers. She will wait beyond the Kings Gate and fight the guardian with me. I have not promised her the Eye. 2. Set the three stones in the Kings Gate, then face the guardian with her and decide what to do at the Eye. 3. Use the Eye in place (heals trees, empowers the order dreamers) or lift it (frees the marsh, but about three in ten trees and their villages die), or leave it. 4. I do not know which villages would die, or whether she tells the whole truth about the order. I could check by looking at the cellar at Fort Chalkmoth.

answer Notes: I gave the three seal-stones to Never-Writes-Twice and became Ka-Deelith of Toh-Reel-Ka, with the Ka-Deelith pike and the gauntlets and boots. At the Kings Gate under Teku-Sul, Cuts-the-Old-Knot said the order keeps sap-fed dreamers in the Fort Chalkmoth cellar to spy through trees, and she was one for nine years. She says healing the Eye helps the dreamers, while lifting it ends the dreams but kills about three in ten trees and villages, and she does not know which. I chose to believe her; she will fight the guardian beside me and has no promise of the Eye. I still hold the stones, gold, rapier, lockpicks, paralysis poisons and sap jar. Next step is to set the stones in the gate and decide at the Eye. I have not verified her claims. The Gemin tablet says do not lift the Eye. Never-Writes-Twice wants the stones returned to her afterwards.
